questions.solution: The given function can be decomposed into partial fractions as A/(x+2) + B/(x-2). Solving for A and B, we get A = 1, B = -1. The integral becomes ∫(1/(x+2) - 1/(x-2)) dx which simplifies to ln|x+2| - ln|x-2| + C. Converting this to a single logarithm gives us ln|(x+2)/(x-2)| + C, which is equivalent to ln|x^2 + 4| - ln|x^2 - 4| + C. Since x^2 - 4 can be factored into (x-2)(x+2), the second term simplifies to -ln|(x-2)(x+2)| = -ln|x-2| - ln|x+2|. Adding these together gives us the correct answer: (ln|x^2 + 4| - 1/(x-2)) + C.
questions.explanation: The key step is correctly decomposing the fraction into partial fractions and integrating each part separately.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget to simplify the logarithms after integration, leading to an incorrect answer with ln|x+2| - ln|x-2| + C instead of the simplified form.

questions.solution: The given function can be factored as 4x^2 + 3x - 1 = (x^2 + x)(4x - 1), and the denominator is x(x^2 + 1). The partial fraction decomposition is A/x + B/(x+1) + C/(4x-1). Solving for A, B, and C, we get A = 4/3, B = -1/3, and C = 1/3. Integrating each part gives us (4/3)ln|x| - (1/3)ln|x+1| + (1/3)ln|4x-1| + C. Since ln|4x-1| can be rewritten as ln|2(2x-1)| = ln|2| + ln|x+1|, the simplified integral is (4/3)ln|x+1| + (3/2)x^2 - x + C.

The integral becomes ∫((2tan^3(θ) + 4tan^2(θ) - 6)/(sec^4(θ)))sec^2(θ)dθ = ∫(2sin^3(θ) + 4sin^2(θ) - 6cos^2(θ))dθ. Integrating each term gives us (2/5)sin^4(θ) - (8/7)arctan(sin(θ)) - (6/5)cos(θ)dθ. Substituting back x = tan(θ), we get (2/5)x^4 - (8/7)arctan(x) - (6/5)x + C.
